scenario: WIBTA if I told my cousin his kid can’t stay in our house? | My cousin (M27) recently moved in with my husband and I. We completely closed of the very large main bedroom and bathroom to create a flatlet for him that’s separate from the house with his own entrance so it’s basically two separate units of one house. Now my cousin has a 2 year old and he’s busy with a custody battle with his ex so he can get to spend more time with his son. I completely support this and really hopes he gets more time with his son. Yesterday my cousin came to ask me if it would be possible for my husband and I to convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son if and when he comes to visit over weekends. There is no access from my cousin’s room into our part of the house and he doesn’t have keys to come and go as he pleases. I understand that the court will be looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him (and to be honest his current room and bathroom is more than big enough) but I’m not comfortable with letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him and I’m not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that’s just the way my family is and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. WIBTA for telling him I will not allow his son to sleep in our house and completely jeopardizing his court case?

My cousin moved in with my husband and me, and we've set up a separate flatlet for him with his own entrance. That means his space is completely separate from ours. He has a 2-year-old son, and he's going through a custody battle with his ex. I support him wanting to spend more time with his son, and I really hope he gets more custody. Now, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son when he comes over weekends. But here's the thing: there's no access from his room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house because my cousin doesn't have access to him, and I don't want to take responsibility for his kid. Plus, the whole family is involved, and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his custody situation to get him more time with his son. I'm wondering if I should tell him I won't allow his son to stay in our house, which could jeopardize his court case. The court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son. His current room and bathroom are more than big enough, but I'm still not comfortable with the arrangement. So, should I say no? On one hand, I support him and want him to have more time with his son. On the other hand, I don't feel comfortable with the setup because he can't access his son's room, and I don't want the responsibility. I'm also worried about how this might affect his custody case if the court sees that he doesn't have a suitable place for his son. I need to weigh the pros and cons. If I say no, it might hurt his case, but if I say yes, I'm putting myself in an uncomfortable position. Maybe there's a middle ground. Could we find another arrangement where his son can stay without me feeling responsible? Or maybe I can talk to him about why I'm uncomfortable and see if he can address those concerns. I also have to consider the family dynamics. Everyone expects me to help, but I have to prioritize my own comfort and boundaries. It's important to communicate my feelings clearly and see if we can find a solution that works for everyone. In the end, I think it's about balancing support for my cousin with my own boundaries. If I can't find a way to make it work without feeling uncomfortable, then it might be better to say no, even if it affects his case. But I should approach the conversation with empathy and openness to find a solution that works best for everyone involved.
